children: Switzerland's upper house voted in favor of bank capital rules that are expected to require UBS Group
to back its foreign units with 90% of common equity Tier 1 capital, Reuters reported on Wednesday.
The decision is said to have dealt a blow to the Swiss lender, who had
lawmakers to soften proposed capital requirements that could significantly raise the bank's operating costs.
UBS Chairman ​Colm Kelleher had reportedly warned last week that the bank could rethink its Swiss base over the capital requirements.
The stock was trading 0.81% lower at $48.79 on the NYSE during pre-market trading.
The government's plan could require UBS

to hold about $20B in additional capital. A central provision would force the bank to support its foreign subsidiaries entirely with CET 1 capital, the most expensive and loss-absorbing form of bank funding.

A parliamentary committee had proposed allowing UBS to meet half the requirement with additional Tier 1 securities, a less costly form of capital. CEO Sergio Ermotti had described the option as difficult but manageable.

And, some lawmakers had expressed support for requiring 90% of the foreign-subsidiary exposure to be backed by CET1 capital. Ermotti had said that proposal would still place an unreasonable burden on the bank.

Finance Minister Karin Keller-Sutter said before the vote that the country could not handle ​a potential collapse of UBS, according to the newswire. "That's why we need to ​set the necessary guidelines."
The bill is now set to move to Switzerland's lower house, with a final decision expected at 2026 end at the earliest, Reuters reported.

title: Swiss upper house votes in favor of UBS backing foreign units with 90% CET1 capital - report
